text: The reconciliation results, the freshness of the 14 data products and the six quality measures stay this service's product output and are published through rwb-reporting's read model; the data lake copy, the INT-19 extract and the nightly decision-log copy are not built in this service.
why: Arch v5 (higher in precedence) removes the data lake and the dashboard connection and gives measures, snapshots and reporting to rwb-reporting.
read: FSD A2.12, A2.19 and A2.20 as the output content, delivered through the reporting service rather than to a lake.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P1-006, CAP-P1-014; Section 6 FR-P1-023, FR-P1-032; Section 9; Section 10
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 2
impact: If the lake returns, a new extract adapter and a new destination are needed in rwb-integration, not in this service.

text: The retention class per data product and recovery table is declared here as versioned data, the archive rule table and the monthly archive run belong to rwb-document, and ACE retains ACE data.
why: Arch v5 slides 16, 41 and 44 give retention to the document service and the ownership map drops the retention rule copy from P1.
read: FSD A2.17 as the retention class requirement, with the archive mechanism owned elsewhere.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P1-011; Section 6 FR-P1-028; Section 8.1; Section 10
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 1 release
impact: A class declared in one service and applied in another needs a reconciliation report so a table cannot drift past its class.

text: Role-level read access per data product is held here; field-level masking rules are held by rwb-access and applied here, and a personal field with no masking row for the role is returned masked.
why: The ownership map gives masking_rule to P4 rwb-access, which owns masking policy at the architecture level.
read: FSD A2.15 split into a role access product here and a masking policy product there, with the default-masked rule kept.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P1-008; Section 6 FR-P1-024, FR-P1-025; Section 9
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 1 release
impact: Two owners of one decision surface; the cached read must be tested for a stale policy.

text: This service builds and publishes the case list rows and holds their publication status; the case list screen and its filters are served by rwb-case over those rows.
why: The ownership map ruling keeps the case list operation and screen with the case service and the daily row set here.
read: FSD A2.18 rows and reconciliation here, screen and operation in the case service.
confirm: Product owner, at the Epic 1 story review
impact: A screen without its rows is a contract dependency, not a build dependency.

text: This service serves the measure snapshot for a business date whose ACE batches are complete; rwb-reporting publishes the baseline and freezes it.
why: Arch v5 slide 44 gives the measure job to rwb-reporting and slide 15 gives this service the snapshot activity.
read: FSD A2.19 as a snapshot duty here and a publication duty in reporting.
confirm: Center of excellence, before the baseline is taken
impact: The frozen baseline must not be written back to this service, or two copies of the baseline exist.

text: This service publishes AceDataReady and AceDataLate on rwb.source-data.events.v1; ACE ingestion is not a producer on a Recovery topic.
why: The architecture event catalogue is first in the precedence order and names this service as producer of both events.
read: FSD A2.14 with the ownership and direction of the architecture catalogue.
confirm: Solution architect, at the event contract review
impact: A wrongly consumed event would leave the morning chain with no trigger.

text: Wave 1 delivers the 16 Section A views, the four extension tables, the dictionary, the reconciliation, the case list and the ledger; the 14 Section B views, the batch-status freshness source and every Tier 2 feature stay behind their flags until the ACE additions land.
why: The ACE additions are not accepted (DL43 open) and a view cannot be created over a table that does not exist.
read: FSD A2.1 and A2.14 with the Section B gate as a flag, not a blocker for the Section A product.
confirm: ACE team lead, on accepting RWB-ACE-001
impact: Freshness, the case list and the reconciliation depend on the batch-status view; if the additions slip, wave 1 shows data products as not stamped.

text: The dictionary is loaded from the corrected mapping: one data product per object family, the physical types the views return, the two personal view fields marked personal, systems of record worded 'ACE (ingested from X)', and the counts 16 Section A and 14 Section B.
why: The functional specification states that its criteria assume the corrected mapping, and the rulings fix the wording and the counts.
read: FSD A2.16 and OQ-P1-03 with the frozen view list taking precedence over the seed.
confirm: Data architect, before the dictionary load
impact: A wrong personal-data marker is a PDPA exposure, not a documentation defect.

text: Freshness is read from the batch-status view only, and where the view is absent a data product is shown as not stamped rather than with an inferred date.
why: The rule that freshness is never inferred from a row count, a file or a view's data date is explicit, and the fallback source is unnamed.
read: FSD A2.14 with a visible 'not stamped' state instead of an inferred business date.
confirm: Solution architect, before system test
impact: A decision could cite a date it does not have; the not-stamped state prevents that.

text: The per-account reconciliation break list is published with the reconciliation result and its read operation, not held in an unowned table.
why: The table the break rows were written to leaves the schema and no target store is confirmed.
read: FSD A2.11 and A2.12 keeping every orphan and every break key visible to the steward and the ACE team.
confirm: Data architect, at the data-model review
impact: A break that is computed but not listed cannot be cleared; the publish hold becomes permanent.

text: This service writes the appraisal stale flag and the age in days on the valuation extension row, with the 365-day rule held as data, until the owning function is assigned.
why: The extension row is owned here and no other writer is named; a second writer would break the one-writer rule.
read: FSD A2.6 carried rule with the writer unresolved.
confirm: Business analyst, P1 and S1, before system test
impact: If the valuation service writes the same two fields, one of them must stop.

text: The four-label classification in this PRD is read from the personal-data markers in the field catalogues: personal fields and the party and contact extension rows as personal data, balances, amounts, offers, debt sale and money as sensitive financial data, case, legal, collateral, documents and metadata as confidential, and no data product as public.
why: Every data product must carry a classification that sets its handling, and the approved scheme is still open.
read: FSD field catalogues and BRD NFR-047 with the markers as the only available evidence.
confirm: Compliance with Security, when DL26 closes
impact: The handling rules follow the label; a wrong label changes who may read a product.

text: This service owns the interaction ledger tables and the write path; the case service serves the case timeline over this service's contract and the integration service writes intake outcomes through the same contract.
why: The source-default ruling puts the interaction ledger here and the case timeline in the case service.
read: FSD and the Epic 1 ledger requirements as one writer, many readers.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P1-012; Section 6 FR-P1-029, FR-P1-030; AC-P1-024
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 1 release
impact: Two ledger writers would make the case history non-authoritative.

text: The data contract, the two Stage 2 data-product copies and the ledger intake rule carry a placeholder field list in this version; their fields, types and keys are fixed at the technical specification review.
why: The tables are named, owned and ruled but no read source lists their fields.
read: Ownership map names and rulings with the field detail deferred to the technical specification.
confirm: Data architect, before wave 2
impact: A story that needs a field cannot reach Done until the list exists.

text: Both entry paths are built: the business-date ready call, idempotent on the date and answered 202, with a status read of RUNNING, DONE or LATE; and the poll of the ACE batch record as the fallback where ACE ingestion is scheduled outside the bank scheduler.
why: The scheduler contract is a recommendation to discuss and the functional specification assumes a poll.
read: Arch v5 slide 32 as the target contract and the FSD poll as the fallback.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P1-017; Section 9; AC-P1-013; Section 12 OQ-P1-13
confirm: Solution architect with the bank platform team, before the integration test
impact: If only one path is built and it is the wrong one, no business date is ever declared ready.

text: This service serves the job, freshness, reconciliation and dictionary operations; the composite route is the edge's and the dashboard shell is the reporting service's.
why: The architecture gives reporting the dashboard and the edge the composite route, while the functional specification lists both screens with this module.
read: FSD screens split into operations here and screen shell elsewhere.
confirm: Solution architect, before Epic 2 acceptance
impact: A screen with an unassigned owner cannot be accepted.

text: This PRD is carried as Draft with an empty approval table, on the reading that the business requirements are the baseline in force and that the product owner and FDA decisions follow.
why: No approval or governance record exists in the converted business requirements, and the run rules remove human approval stops.
read: The requirement substance is unchanged and the approval is a later gate, not a precondition for the document.
confirm: Product owner and FDA, at the requirements approval gate
impact: Nothing in the build may be treated as approved until the gate is passed.

text: The release dates are carried unchanged and marked tentative: 30 November 2026 for Epic 1, 31 December 2026 for Epic 2, 30 June 2027 for Epic 8.
why: Dates are tentative in this run and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: BRD Program v4 section 8 and the story rules on tentative dates.
confirm: Programme office, at each release gate
impact: A slice may move with its epic; the requirement stays.

text: This document is version 1 of the PRD family for the service: no earlier PRD exists in the folder.
why: The version is the highest of the family plus one, and the folder holds no earlier version.
read: A new file, not a copy of a source document.
confirm: Document controller, at the next version
impact: None; the next version is v2.

text: The service is wave 1, Epic 1 releases as business epic EP01 in wave 1, and the Stage 2 data products are the only part of this product that ships in Epic 2 (EP02, wave 2).
why: Arch v5 slide 41 and the ownership map put the service in wave 1, and the business-epic wave map puts EP02 in wave 2.
read: Epic 1 as the foundation release, Epic 2 as the first increment that needs a new data product from here.
confirm: Programme office, at wave planning
impact: A story pulled earlier would break the service-created-with-its-epic rule.
